title: Stowaway labbook: context fragments & deployment notes
content:
Quick purpose: a messy, portable brain-dump on what I read this sprint about context fragmentation, sparse-KV, and deployment considerations for private/Dedicated modes. Meant as a personal labbook + TODO list — not final.

Top-level takeaways (TL;DR):
- Fragmentation is both a model/utilization problem and a systems problem: too many short, overlapping contexts kills cache hit rates and increases per-token compute.
- Sparse-KV (sharded/hashed key stores + approximate lookups) looks promising to keep working set small but adds retrieval noise — needs eval hooks on generation quality.
- Deployment constraints (VPC/private) complicate global caching/backplane ideas: prefer local cache tiers + async propagation for bounded staleness.

Papers / links skimmed (notes inline):
1) "Compact KV for Long Contexts" (arXiv) — strategy: chunk-level fingerprints + bloom filters per shard.
   - Idea: maintain small bloom per GPU to cheaply filter miss candidates before remote lookup.
   - Ops note: bloom false-positive rate -> extra cross-machine RPCs; tune by workload.

2) Sparse-associative memory blog post (conf blog) — approximate hashing vs learned retrieval.
   - Learned retrieval yields better semantic hits but needs periodic reindexing. For Dedicated we can schedule reindex jobs during low SLO windows.

3) "Eviction policies for streaming KV" (workshop paper) — LRU vs LFU vs adaptive hybrid.
   - Practical: LRU works fine for stable sessions; for mixed short/long sessions, weighted recency (decay) gives better overall hit rate.

Field notes / experiment ideas to run in next sprint:
- Small replay: take 1000 real customer sessions (anonymized) and simulate KV hits under different shard counts and bloom sizes. Metric: effective tokens served locally vs remote.
- Quality probe: for the same sessions, simulate approximate retrieval (top-k approx) and measure generation logits divergence + human-check hallucination rate on 50 sampled prompts.
- Deployment test: run two configs in private deployment: local-only cache (no cross-host sync) vs low-latency eventual sync. Measure hit rate, p50/p95 latency, and tail SLO violations.

Notes-to-self on instrumentation:
- Add a lightweight tag in traces: kv_hit_type = {local_exact, local_approx, remote} so we can compute cost/quality tradeoffs.
- Export per-session cache-hit curves to Console; add view to surface sessions where hit rate drops < 20%.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How much generation quality degrades with top-k approx retrieval? We need small human evals and automatic regen-diff metrics (KL/logit-norm).
- Privacy: if we shard by customer id, cross-customer caching disappears. Can we use tenant-local shards plus a shared cold-lookup with strict gating? Need legal/infosec signoff for any cross-tenant material.
- Cost: bloom filters reduce remote RPCs but increase memory usage per GPU. Tradeoff curve must be plotted for typical model footprints (LLama- style 7B vs 70B).

Deployment checklist (practical):
- Config knobs endpoint: kv.enabled, kv.mode = {local, hybrid, global}, bloom.size, shard.count, approx.topk. Default: hybrid with low approx topk for hosted; local for private by default.
- Safe rollback: ability to toggle kv.mode per-customer route and fallback to remote full-context generation.
- Canary: start with 1% of traffic, monitor hallucination/regression alerts tied to eval prompt set.

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Latent fingerprinting: store compact embeddings + time-decay so that recent fragments are prioritized for session continuity. Could combine with sparse-KV for candidate set.
- Stale buffer: for Private deployments, let some hosts keep a small ring buffer of last N shards they served; if a remote miss occurs, try stale-first to avoid remote cold-call.

Quick notes on related internal threads/PRs:
- PR #88 on github: small raft for kv replica placement (need to rebase, tests failing on sim).
- Slack: CACHE-ops-thread: argued for per-route bloom tuning; flagged by SRE re memory overhead.

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Prep simulation harness: dataset extraction (ask infra for safe anonymized dump).
- [ ] Implement kv_hit_type trace tag + Console dashboard prototype.
- [ ] Run 50-sample human eval comparing exact vs approx retrieval outputs.
- [ ] Draft short one-pager for product: "KV cache modes & recommended defaults" (aim to share with solutions engineering).

Random scribbles / heuristics I keep repeating:
- Short sessions: prioritize low-latency, disable heavy reindexing.
- Long sessions: invest in higher-quality retrievals and periodic reindexing.
- When in doubt: prefer local-safe defaults for Private deployments to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Notes to self: when I come back to this, start by extracting 1) session length distribution, 2) median overlap between successive requests, 3) token reuse fraction. Those stats will drive shard sizing and bloom filter configs.

End of page — more later.
